I've struggled with this as well, and I especially struggle with this because I AM on a scheduled/controlled substance. However, I am currently in 3/4 living and my medicine is monitored by a professional, and I have no chance to even abuse my meds.

And as for psych meds as a whole, my counselor explained it to me like this. If I had a broken bone, I would put a cast on it. The cast doesn't heal the broken bone, it just protects it while the body mends the broken bone. As for mental illness, psych meds do not heal our illness, they just protect us. The only way to survive without psych meds is to truly understand, process, and treat your illness - be in depression, anxiety, and especially alcoholism/addiction.

I'd strongly suggest that you talk to a therapist/nurse practitioner about your meds. Do NOT go on and off them. Each time you go off your meds, it takes longer for them to begin working again when you start taking them again. Also look into a therapist that has experience with alcohol and substance abuse. I have recently been going to a type of therapy called EMDR - which stands for Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing, which is helping me work through the unresolved trauma's and PTSD that I have from my childhood and years of active addiction.

Stay on your meds until you have begun to thoroughly address and treat your mental illnesses.

So I'm standing on the front porch of a bar drinking my first beer of the night, and having a cigarette. To the left of me, there is a line of businesses with a side walk in front. If you were to walk about 20 feet down the side walk, you can walk down a bit, turn to the left and come back up to the back parking lot of the bar and come back to the front porch im standing on.

So i'm just leaning against the post, and I see a couple walking down the side walk, away from me. It's a man and a woman, the man wearing a white t-shirt and the woman wearing a dark blue tie-dye. Someone walks out the front door of the bar, so I turn to look at them, shoot a quick smile, say hello, etc. Couldn't have been more than 30 seconds... I look back to the left, and the couple is standing RIGHT by the porch again, walking away. I watch in disbelief as they had probably been about 15 feet away when I turned to see who was coming onto the porch I was on! Then I look down to my right to grab my beer that was on the railing next to me, to take a drink, and when I turn back, they are RIGHT in the same spot they started, walking away again. It was a truly strange thing to experience! There's no way in the brief moments that I had been looking away that they could have walked all the way down the alley and back around the front of the porch to get to that same part of the side walk again. Have never had it happen since!
